title: Oil Tops $100 as Iran Vows to Escalate War, Trump Says US Will Win
description:
Oil climbs above $100 a barrel as the war with Iran escalates and Tehran says it has no intention of backing down. President Donald Trump says the US will win the war with Iran and suggests the Strait of Hormuz should be renamed the “Trump Strait,” while an Iranian official says Iran is ready to escalate the conflict.
Brent crude rallies as the war disrupts energy supplies and fuels renewed inflation concerns. OPEC output slumps as the conflict curbs Saudi flows, with Saudi production plunging by more than 1 million barrels. Iraq, meanwhile, is seeking a significant increase in its OPEC production quota.
Asian stocks fall as surging oil prices revive inflation fears, while the dollar hovers near seven-month lows. Investors are also weighing higher crude prices against the US Treasury’s buyback plans.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s $6 billion buyback plan disappoints investors. His comments on Japan are also raising expectations around monetary policy that the Bank of Japan may struggle to meet, while BOJ official Masu says further rate hikes are needed to complete policy normalization.
The European Central Bank is expected to raise interest rates today as policymakers confront renewed inflation pressures.
Apple enters the foldable-phone market with prices starting at $1,999 as the company positions the iPhone as a personal intelligence hub. Apple’s new iPhone duo reaches $3,199, setting an industry record, as the company prepares for a broader run of product releases.
President Trump floats a $5,000 payment to US adults if Republicans win the midterm elections.
SoftBank plans to repay a $40 billion bridge loan tied to its OpenAI stake.
Shipping nations sound the alarm over an increasingly fragmented global trading system as geopolitical tensions disrupt shipping routes and international commerce.
Dow is weighing an exit from its $20 billion Saudi chemicals venture, while Mubadala backs Luckin Coffee.
Dangote refinery cuts its debt to $5.7 billion ahead of its planned IPO, while Mozambique’s dollar bonds climb to their highest level in six years. Guests includes Carole Nakhle, Crystol Energy CEO, Deepak Mehra, Commercial Bank of Dubai Chief Economist and Richard Windsor, Radio Free Mobile Founder.

Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. Live from Dubai, we bring you the latest global markets and analysis, plus news-making interviews, with a special focus on MEA. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg.
